title: Home & neighbourhood
goal: Rent a room or flat in Kathmandu, ask about water and power, report what is broken and get the landlord to have it fixed, pay the bills, and deal politely with neighbours and noise.
intro:
Sooner or later you'll live in a **डेरा** — rented rooms, usually in a house where the landlord (**घरबेटी**) lives downstairs. That means talking about rent, the water supply, gas cylinders, power cuts, leaking taps and the neighbours' dog.

This unit gives you two tools. First, **complaining politely but firmly**: naming the problem, saying how long it has been going on (धारा बिग्रेको तीन दिन **भयो** 'the tap has been broken for three days'), and softening your request so the landlord stays on your side. Second, the **causative** — not doing a job yourself but **getting it done**: मर्मत **गराउनु** 'to get it repaired', मिस्त्रीलाई **बनाउन लगाउनु** 'to get the repairman to fix it'.

vocab.note: डेरा गरेर बस्नु / डेरामा बस्नु "to live in rented rooms"; डेरा सर्नु "to move house". A renter is a डेरावाल (ḍerāwāl).
Also घरधनी (gharadhani). Addressed as दाइ, दिदी, or अंकल/आन्टी — never by the word घरबेटी.
Often just भाडा. भाडा तिर्नु / बुझाउनु "to pay the rent".
A whole floor with its own kitchen. Rooms without one are just कोठा.
Formal Nepali: धरौटी (dharauṭi) "deposit".
Also "compromise": सम्झौता गर्नु.
In speech the power is often just बत्ती: बत्ती गयो "the power went".
The water board is खानेपानी too. Drinking water is usually bought in 20-litre जार.
जारको पानी "jar water", delivered to the door.
Also the old stone spouts (ढुङ्गेधारा) of the Kathmandu valley.
The black plastic tank on every roof.
When the piped water fails, you pay for a ट्याङ्कर to fill the roof tank.
ग्यास सकियो "the gas has run out"; ग्यास भराउनु "to get the cylinder refilled".
बत्तीको बिल, पानीको बिल, इन्टरनेटको बिल.
Tenants often pay by their own sub-meter: मिटरअनुसार "according to the meter".
Where washing is dried and tanks stand. A sloping roof is छाना.
A boundary wall round a compound is पर्खाल (parkhāl).
छिमेक "neighbourhood"; छिमेकी देश "neighbouring country".
Old Kathmandu is a patchwork of टोल, each with its own name, shrine and festivals.
गुनासो गर्नु "to complain". A formal written complaint is उजुरी.
Specify the trade: पानीको मिस्त्री / प्लम्बर (plumber), बिजुलीको मिस्त्री (electrician).
धारा चुहियो "the tap leaked"; छानाबाट पानी चुहिन्छ "the roof leaks".

vocab.en: to pay (rent, a bill), hand over; to explain
vocab.note: Causative of बुझ्नु "to understand / receive". भाडा बुझाएँ "I paid the rent".
One of the most useful verbs in Nepali: मिलाइदिनुहोस् "please sort it out".
बल्ब फेर्नु "to change a bulb"; लुगा फेर्नु "to change clothes".
कुकुर रातभरि भुक्छ "the dog barks all night".

vocab.en: to be made; to get fixed
vocab.note: अझै बनेको छैन "it still hasn't been fixed". Its partner बनाउनु means "to make, to fix".

phrases.note: Look for handwritten कोठा भाडामा पाइन्छ signs taped to walls and poles.

phrases.note: The first question every Kathmandu tenant asks.

phrases.en: There's no water in the tap.

phrases.note: Polite but clear. To a friend: छिट्टै मिलाइदेऊ न।

phrases.note: The कि at the end makes it a gentle "would you mind…?".

phrases.en: When should I pay the rent?
When does the rubbish truck come?

phrases.roman: hāmi arko mahinā ḍerā sardai chhauṃ.

grammar.title: Complaining politely but firmly
grammar.body:
A good complaint in Nepali has three parts: **what is wrong**, **how long it has been going on**, and **a soft but clear request**. Shouting gets you nowhere; calm persistence does.

**1. Say what's wrong.** Use the simple past or the -एको छ perfect, which you already know: पानी **आएन** 'the water didn't come', बत्ती **गएको छ** 'the power is out', ग्यास **सकियो** 'the gas has run out', धारा **बिग्रियो** 'the tap broke'. For something still going on use -इरहेको छ: धारा **चुहिरहेको छ** 'the tap is leaking'. For something that keeps happening use **-इरहन्छ** 'keeps on…': बत्ती **गइरहन्छ** 'the power keeps going off'.

**2. Say how long — the '-एको … भयो' pattern.** Nepali says 'it has become three days since X happened':

- धारा **बिग्रेको** तीन दिन **भयो** — 'The tap has been broken for three days.'
- पानी **नआएको** एक हप्ता **भयो** — 'There's been no water for a week' (lit. 'it has become a week of the water not coming').
- मैले **भनेको** दुई हप्ता **भइसक्यो** — 'It's been two weeks since I told you.'

The verb takes **-एको** (negative **न-…-एको**), then the length of time, then **भयो** (or the sharper **भइसक्यो** 'already'). **अझै** + negative perfect is the other key word: अझै **बनेको छैन** 'it still hasn't been fixed'.

**3. Ask softly.** Use the 'for me' form -इदिनु from unit 18 and add a softener:

- मिलाइदिनुहोस् **न** — 'please sort it out' (न makes it friendly, not pushy)
- मिलाइदिनुहुन्छ **कि**? — 'would you mind sorting it out?'
- मिलाइदिनुभए **राम्रो हुन्थ्यो** — 'it would be great if you could sort it out' (the most diplomatic)

To get firmer without being rude, keep the polite verb but add facts and time: मैले दुई पटक भनिसकेँ, **तर** अझै बनेको छैन। **आज** मिलाइदिनुहोस् न। Getting firmer never means dropping from तपाईं to तिमी — that would sound like picking a fight.

examples.en: The tap has been broken for a week.
There's been no water for three days.

examples.native: मैले दुई पटक भनिसकेँ, तर अझै बनेको छैन।
examples.roman: maile dui paṭak bhanisakeṃ, tara ajhai baneko chhaina.
examples.en: I've told you twice already, but it still hasn't been fixed.
It would be great if you could send a repairman.
The noise goes on until midnight.

grammar.title: Causatives revisited: getting something done
grammar.body:
When you don't fix something yourself but **get it done**, Nepali uses a **causative**. There are two ways.

**1. The -आउनु causative.** Many verbs have a partner ending in **-आउनु** that means 'make/have someone do it'. You already know several: देख्नु 'see' → **देखाउनु** 'show', बुझ्नु 'understand' → **बुझाउनु** 'explain; hand over', पढ्नु 'study' → **पढाउनु** 'teach'. The one you need most is **गर्नु → गराउनु** 'have done', used with a noun of action:

- मर्मत **गर्नु** 'to repair' → मर्मत **गराउनु** 'to get repaired'
- सफा **गर्नु** 'to clean' → सफा **गराउनु** 'to get cleaned'
- जाँच **गर्नु** 'to check' → जाँच **गराउनु** 'to get checked'

It conjugates like any verb: गराएँ 'I had it done', गराउनुभयो 'you/he (polite) had it done', गराउनुपर्छ 'it needs to be done'.

**2. -न लगाउनु 'make / get someone to do'.** Put the main verb in its **-न** form and add **लगाउनु**. The person who does the work takes **-लाई**:

- **मिस्त्रीलाई** धारा **फेर्न लगाउनुहोस्** — 'Get the repairman to replace the tap.'
- घरबेटीले **मलाई** एडभान्स **तिर्न लगाउनुभयो** — 'The landlord made me pay an advance.'

**The trap.** To your landlord, **मर्मत गरिदिनुहोस्** asks *him* to repair it himself, which can sound odd; **मर्मत गराइदिनुहोस्** 'please get it repaired (for me)' is what you mean. Both causatives combine happily with the 'for me' -इदिनु: गराइदिनुहोस्, फेर्न लगाइदिनुहोस्.

'I need to get X done' is simply **X गराउनुपर्छ**: मलाई ट्याङ्की सफा गराउनुपर्छ।

examples.en: The landlord got the tap repaired.
Please get the repairman to fix the door.
The tank needs to be cleaned.

examples.native: उहाँले मलाई दुई महिनाको एडभान्स तिर्न लगाउनुभयो।
examples.roman: uhāṃle malāi dui mahināko eḍbhāns tirna lagāunubhayo.
examples.en: She made me pay two months' advance.

dialogue.title: No water, again
dialogue.setting: Anu rents the top floor of a house in Baneshwor, Kathmandu. She goes downstairs to see her landlady, Sharmila aunty.

lines.speaker: Anu
lines.native: आन्टी, नमस्ते। एकछिन कुरा गर्न मिल्छ?
lines.roman: ānṭi, namaste. ekchhin kurā garna milchha?
lines.en: Hello, aunty. Have you got a minute?

lines.speaker: Sharmila
lines.native: आऊ आऊ, बस। के भयो? अनुहार त उदास छ नि।
lines.roman: āu āu, basa. ke bhayo? anuhār ta udās chha ni.
lines.en: Come in, sit down. What's up? You look miserable.

lines.speaker: Anu
lines.native: माथि पानी नआएको तीन दिन भयो, आन्टी। ट्याङ्की खाली छ।
lines.roman: māthi pāni naāeko tin din bhayo, ānṭi. ṭyāṅki khāli chha.
lines.en: There's been no water upstairs for three days, aunty. The tank's empty.

lines.speaker: Sharmila
lines.native: ओहो, मेलम्चीको पानी यो हप्ता आएकै छैन। के गर्ने?
lines.roman: oho, Melamchiko pāni yo haptā āekai chhaina. ke garne?
lines.en: Oh dear, the Melamchi water hasn't come at all this week. What can you do?

lines.speaker: Anu
lines.native: एउटा ट्याङ्कर मगाइदिनुभए राम्रो हुन्थ्यो। नुहाउनै पाइएन!
lines.roman: euṭā ṭyāṅkar magāidinubhae rāmro hunthyo. nuhāunai pāiena!
lines.en: It'd be great if you could order a tanker. I haven't even been able to shower!

lines.speaker: Sharmila
lines.native: हुन्छ, म आजै ट्याङ्कर मगाउँछु। अरू केही?
lines.roman: hunchha, ma ājai ṭyāṅkar magāunchhu. aru kehi?
lines.en: OK, I'll order a tanker today. Anything else?

lines.speaker: Anu
lines.native: अनि बाथरुमको धारा पनि चुहिरहेको छ। मैले अघिल्लो हप्ता पनि भनेको थिएँ।
lines.roman: ani bāthrumko dhārā pani chuhiraheko chha. maile aghillo haptā pani bhaneko thieṃ.
lines.en: And the bathroom tap is leaking too. I told you last week as well.

lines.speaker: Sharmila
lines.native: हो र? मैले त बिर्सेछु। भोलि मिस्त्रीलाई बोलाएर फेर्न लगाउँछु।
lines.roman: ho ra? maile ta birsechhu. bholi mistrilāi bolāera pherna lagāunchhu.
lines.en: Really? I must have forgotten. Tomorrow I'll call the plumber and get him to replace it.

lines.speaker: Anu
lines.native: धन्यवाद आन्टी। अनि यो महिनाको भाडा, खल्तीबाट पठाऊँ कि नगद दिऊँ?
lines.roman: dhanyabād ānṭi. ani yo mahināko bhāḍā, Khaltibāṭa paṭhāuṃ ki nagad diuṃ?
lines.en: Thanks, aunty. And this month's rent — shall I send it by Khalti or give you cash?

lines.speaker: Sharmila
lines.native: खल्तीमै पठाऊ। बत्तीको बिल चाहिँ मिटर हेरेर पछि भनुँला।
lines.roman: Khaltimai paṭhāu. battiko bil chāhiṃ miṭar herera pachhi bhanuṃlā.
lines.en: Send it on Khalti. As for the electricity bill, I'll check the meter and tell you later.

lines.speaker: Sharmila
lines.native: तर एउटा कुरा: हिजो राति तिम्रा साथीहरूको आवाज अलि धेरै आयो है।
lines.roman: tara euṭā kurā: hijo rāti timrā sāthiharuko āwāj ali dherai āyo hai.
lines.en: But one thing: last night your friends were a bit loud, you know.

lines.speaker: Anu
lines.native: सरी आन्टी! अर्को पटकदेखि दस बजेपछि चुपचाप।
lines.roman: sari ānṭi! arko paṭakdekhi das bajepachhi chupchāp.
lines.en: Sorry, aunty! From next time, total silence after ten.

lines.speaker: Sharmila
lines.native: हाहा, ठीक छ। पानी आएपछि म बोलाउँछु।
lines.roman: hāhā, ṭhik chha. pāni āepachhi ma bolāunchhu.
lines.en: Haha, all right. I'll give you a shout when the water comes.

culture:
Most young people in Kathmandu who aren't living with family live in a **डेरा** — a couple of rooms in a family house, with the **घरबेटी** downstairs. That makes the landlord half neighbour, half aunt: they will ask where you were last night, send up a plate of food at Dashain, and have opinions about your guests. Call them **आन्टी/अंकल** or **दाइ/दिदी** and use **तपाईं** (a landlady may well call you **तिमी**, as Sharmila does — that's affection, not rudeness). Many houses have rules: the gate is locked at night, no loud music late, and sometimes no cooking meat on certain days.

**Water** is the big issue. Piped water from the खानेपानी board (and the Melamchi project) arrives only on certain days, sometimes at 4 a.m., and is pumped up to the **ट्याङ्की** on the roof. When it fails, people buy a **ट्याङ्कर** of water, and drinking water comes in 20-litre **जार**. So ask **पानी कस्तो आउँछ?** before you sign anything. Cooking is on **LPG cylinders** — keep a spare, because ग्यास सकियो always happens mid-meal.

Rent is usually paid monthly, now often through **eSewa or Khalti** (Nepal's payment wallets), with one or two months' **एडभान्स**. Electricity is often split by sub-**मिटर**. When something breaks, tenants report it to the landlord, who calls the मिस्त्री. Complaints work best when they are calm, specific and repeated — and a neighbour's complaint is usually passed on through the landlord rather than face to face.

tip.title: Renting in Kathmandu
tip.body:
- You rent a **डेरा** (rooms) or a **फ्ल्याट** from a **घरबेटी**; 'to live in rented rooms' is **डेरा गरेर बस्नु**.
- Ask the price: **महिनाको कति हो?** · and the advance: एडभान्स **कति महिनाको**?
- 'How much a month' = **महिनाको**, 'how many months' advance' = **कति महिनाको** — the -को does the work.
- Use **तपाईं** with the landlord, even if they're young.

sentences.en: I live in rented rooms in Kathmandu.
Excuse me, are there rooms to rent here?
I need two rooms and a kitchen.

sentences.native: यो फ्ल्याटको घरभाडा महिनाको कति हो?
sentences.roman: yo phlyāṭko gharbhāḍā mahināko kati ho?
sentences.en: How much is the rent on this flat a month?
How many months' advance do I have to pay?
The landlord lives downstairs, we live upstairs.
The agreement is for one year.

sentences.native: यहाँ पानी कस्तो आउँछ, दिनहुँ आउँछ?
sentences.roman: yahāṃ pāni kasto āunchha, dinahuṃ āunchha?
sentences.en: What's the water like here — does it come every day?

sentences.native: पानी हप्तामा दुई पटक मात्र आउँछ।
sentences.roman: pāni haptāmā dui paṭak mātra āunchha.
sentences.en: The water only comes twice a week.

sentences.native: घरभाडा अलि महँगो भयो, अलि घटाउनुहुन्छ कि?
sentences.roman: gharbhāḍā ali mahaṃgo bhayo, ali ghaṭāunuhunchha ki?
sentences.en: The rent's a bit too high — could you bring it down a little?

tip.title: It's been three days! -एको … भयो
tip.body:
- Say what's wrong in the past: पानी **आएन**, बत्ती **गएको छ**, ग्यास **सकियो**.
- Say how long: verb in **-एको** + time + **भयो**: बत्ती **गएको** दुई घण्टा भयो 'the power has been off for two hours'.
- Negative: **न-** in front: पानी **नआएको** तीन दिन भयो 'no water for three days'.
- Sharper: **भइसक्यो** 'already'.

sentences.en: There's been no water in the tap since this morning.
The power has been out for two hours.

sentences.native: ट्याङ्कीमा पानी नआएको तीन दिन भयो।
sentences.roman: ṭyāṅkimā pāni naāeko tin din bhayo.
sentences.en: No water has come into the tank for three days.
The gas ran out two days ago already!

sentences.native: बिजुली गएको एक घण्टा भयो, कहिले आउँछ?
sentences.roman: bijuli gaeko ek ghanṭā bhayo, kahile āunchha?
sentences.en: The electricity's been off for an hour — when's it coming back?
For drinking water, we buy jars.

sentences.native: ग्यास सकियो, अब खाना कसरी पकाउने?
sentences.roman: gyās sakiyo, aba khānā kasari pakāune?
sentences.en: The gas has run out — how are we going to cook now?
Oh, the jar water has run out too.
Don't drink the tap water, OK?

sentences.native: तीन दिन भइसक्यो, ट्याङ्की अझै खाली छ।
sentences.roman: tin din bhaisakyo, ṭyāṅki ajhai khāli chha.
sentences.en: It's been three days already and the tank is still empty.

tip.title: Polite but firm
tip.body:
- Still going on: **-इरहेको छ** — धारा **चुहिरहेको छ**. Keeps happening: **-इरहन्छ**.
- 'Still not': **अझै** + **-एको छैन** — अझै **बनेको छैन**.
- Ask softly: मिलाइदिनुहोस् **न** · मिलाइदिनुहुन्छ **कि**? · मिलाइदिनुभए **राम्रो हुन्थ्यो**.
- Firmer = more facts and time, never तिमी.

sentences.en: The kitchen tap is leaking too.
When it rains, water leaks through the roof.

sentences.native: मैले दुई पटक भनेँ, तर अझै बनेको छैन।
sentences.roman: maile dui paṭak bhaneṃ, tara ajhai baneko chhaina.
sentences.en: I've said it twice, but it still hasn't been fixed.
The power keeps going off — I wonder what the problem is.
Would you mind sending the repairman today?

sentences.native: ढोका बन्द हुँदैन, मिलाइदिनुभए राम्रो हुन्थ्यो।
sentences.roman: ḍhokā banda hundaina, milāidinubhae rāmro hunthyo.
sentences.en: The door won't shut; it'd be great if you could fix it.
Could you fix this window for me, please?
Apparently the repairman is coming tomorrow morning.

sentences.native: धारा चुहिएको एक हप्ता भयो, छिट्टै मिलाइदिनुहोस् न।
sentences.roman: dhārā chuhieko ek haptā bhayo, chhiṭṭai milāidinuhos na.
sentences.en: The tap's been leaking for a week — please sort it out soon.

lessons.title: Getting the landlord to fix it

tip.title: Get it done: गराउनु, -न लगाउनु
tip.body:
- **गर्नु → गराउनु** 'have done': मर्मत **गराउनु** 'get repaired', सफा **गराउनु** 'get cleaned'.
- **-न लगाउनु** 'get someone to do': मिस्त्री**लाई** धारा **फेर्न लगाउनु**. The worker takes **-लाई**.
- To the landlord: मर्मत **गराइदिनुहोस्** 'get it repaired for me' — not मर्मत गरिदिनुहोस्, which asks him to do it himself.

sentences.en: Please get this tap repaired.
The landlord got the door repaired.
Get the repairman to replace the old tap.

sentences.native: मैले बिजुलीको मिस्त्रीलाई बत्ती हेर्न लगाएँ।
sentences.roman: maile bijuliko mistrilāi batti herna lagāeṃ.
sentences.en: I got the electrician to look at the lights.
Tomorrow I'll get the repairman to fix the door.
The tank on the roof needs to be cleaned.

sentences.native: यो महिना मैले कोठा सफा गराएँ।
sentences.roman: yo mahinā maile koṭhā saphā garāeṃ.
sentences.en: This month I had the room cleaned.
How much will it cost to get it repaired?
Am I allowed to dry clothes on the roof?

sentences.native: यो भित्ता फोहोर भयो, सफा गराउनुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: yo bhittā phohor bhayo, saphā garāunuparchha.
sentences.en: This wall has got dirty; it needs to be cleaned.

sentences.native: पानी आएन भने ट्याङ्करको पानी किन्नुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: pāni āena bhane ṭyāṅkarko pāni kinnuparchha.
sentences.en: If the water doesn't come, we have to buy tanker water.
In the evening you can see the mountains from the roof.
How much was this month's bill?

sentences.native: बत्तीको बिल मिटर हेरेर तिर्ने हो।
sentences.roman: battiko bil miṭar herera tirne ho.
sentences.en: The electricity bill is paid according to the meter.
The rent has to be paid in the first week of the month.
But I paid the rent yesterday.

sentences.native: यो बिल कसले तिर्ने, तपाईं कि म?
sentences.roman: yo bil kasle tirne, tapāiṃ ki ma?
sentences.en: Who pays this bill, you or me?

sentences.native: फोहोर गाडी हप्तामा दुई पटक आउँछ।
sentences.roman: phohor gāḍi haptāmā dui paṭak āunchha.
sentences.en: The rubbish truck comes twice a week.

sentences.native: फोहोर गाडी आउँदा बाहिर फोहोर लैजानुहोस्।
sentences.roman: phohor gāḍi āundā bāhira phohor laijānuhos.
sentences.en: When the rubbish truck comes, take the rubbish out.
Is the water bill included in the rent too?

lessons.title: Neighbours and moving

tip.title: Keeping the peace with neighbours
tip.body:
- Start soft: आवाज **अलि** कम गरिदिनुहुन्छ **कि**? — the अलि and कि do the softening.
- Add facts: राति बाह्र बजेसम्म, **हरेक** दिन.
- Neighbours are दाइ, दिदी, आन्टी — and a complaint often goes **through the landlord**: घरबेटीलाई गुनासो गर्नु.
- Moving out: **डेरा सर्नु**.

new: हामी अर्को महिना डेरा सर्दै छौँ।

sentences.native: हाम्रो टोल शान्त छ, छिमेकी पनि राम्रा छन्।
sentences.roman: hāmro ṭol sānta chha, chhimeki pani rāmrā chhan.
sentences.en: Our neighbourhood is quiet, and the neighbours are nice too.

sentences.native: दिदी, आवाज अलि कम गरिदिनुहुन्छ कि? बच्चा सुत्दै छ।
sentences.roman: didi, āwāj ali kam garidinuhunchha ki? bachchā sutdai chha.
sentences.en: Could you keep the noise down a bit? The baby's asleep.
The neighbours' dog barks a lot at night.

sentences.native: कुकुर भुकेको आवाजले म सुत्न सकिनँ।
sentences.roman: kukur bhukeko āwājle ma sutna sakinaṃ.
sentences.en: I couldn't sleep because of the dog barking.

sentences.native: हरेक राति एघार बजेसम्म आवाज आइरहन्छ।
sentences.roman: harek rāti eghāra bajesamma āwāj āirahanchha.
sentences.en: Every night the noise goes on until eleven.
I complained to the landlord.

sentences.native: यो टोलमा सबै जना सबैलाई चिन्छन्।
sentences.roman: yo ṭolmā sabai janā sabailāi chinchhan.
sentences.en: In this neighbourhood everyone knows everyone.

sentences.native: हामी अर्को महिना पाटनतिर डेरा सर्दै छौँ।
sentences.roman: hāmi arko mahinā Pāṭantira ḍerā sardai chhauṃ.
sentences.en: We're moving to a place near Patan next month.

sentences.native: डेरा सर्नुअघि घरबेटीलाई एक महिना पहिले भन्नुपर्छ।
sentences.roman: ḍerā sarnuaghi gharbeṭilāi ek mahinā pahile bhannuparchha.
sentences.en: Before moving out you have to tell the landlord a month ahead.
